headlineOptions: Every city decision, explained in five minutes, with a source for every fact.
Know what your council is deciding, how it may affect you, and when you can have a say.
AI drafts it. Your staff approve it. Every fact links to its page.
hero.subhead: Municipal Agents reads a city's own documents and turns a proposed decision into a plain-language brief: what's proposed, how it may affect you, and when you can have a say. Code checks every quote against its page, a named staff member approves every statement, and every step goes on a public record anyone can verify.
hero.secondaryCta: Talk to us about a 90-day pilot

features.title: Every fact has its page
features.body: Click any figure to open the source page with the quote highlighted. If a quote can't be found on the page it cites, the statement is never shown as verified.

features.title: Staff approve before anyone sees it
features.body: Agents draft. Clerks and communications staff approve, edit or reject each statement, then publish under their own name. Until then, the brief says it's a draft.

features.title: A record that can't be edited quietly
features.body: Every brief, approval, question and answer is added to a hash-chained public record. Anyone can check the chain in their browser.

features.title: Have your say, on time
features.body: A timeline of the decision with the next chance to speak, write in or answer a survey, plus the deadline, the contact and an add-to-calendar button.

features.title: Lenses on the same decision
features.body: Transit access gaps, lifecycle cost per household, the city's own commitments, and housing from approval to construction, all computed from open data with the method shown.

features.title: Plain words, for everyone
features.body: Briefs aim for a grade 8 reading level, measured and shown. Designed for WCAG 2.2 AA. Read it in 11 languages; machine translations are labelled.

forWhom.title: Understand it before it's decided
forWhom.body: See what's being decided near you and how it may affect renters, riders, seniors, students, parents or business owners. Find the next date you can take part. You don't need an account, and nothing tracks you.

forWhom.title: Start from a checked draft, not a blank page
forWhom.body: Each statement arrives with its quote and page side by side. Approve, edit or reject in one place, and publish under your name with a record of who approved what.

forWhom.title: One neutral, sourced link
forWhom.body: Lenses you can recognize, with methods and inputs cited. Send constituents a brief that lays out trade-offs on both sides and gives the dates to take part.

faq.a: No municipality yet. Municipal Agents is a working prototype built at CIVIC Hack 2026 from public Waterloo Region documents and open data. We're looking for our first pilot municipalities.

faq.q: Is this the city's official notice?
faq.a: No. Every page says so and links to the official notice, which always prevails. Municipal Agents explains a decision; it doesn't replace legal notice or the city's consultation.

faq.q: Can the AI get things wrong?
faq.a: Yes, which is why it never gets the last word. Code, not a model, checks that every quote is on the page it cites. Sentences with figures that no checked statement supports are removed from answers. A named staff member approves each statement before it's published, and residents can report errors.
City staff. Agents produce a draft; a clerk or communications officer approves, edits or rejects each statement and publishes under their name. The approval is added to the public record.

No, by design. Residents don't need an account, and there are no tracking scripts. Questions are logged with no identifier, and IP addresses are kept in memory only for rate limiting, never written. Please don't type personal details into a question, because questions are part of the public record.

faq.q: Where is data stored, and where does the AI run?
faq.a: The prototype stores its record in Toronto and uses a US-hosted AI model. City and Region plans run the model in Canada or on the city's own infrastructure. Only public documents and residents' questions are sent to the model.

faq.q: Is it accessible, and is it available in French?
faq.a: It's designed to WCAG 2.2 AA, beyond Ontario's WCAG 2.0 AA requirement; an independent audit comes before the first paid launch. French is included in every plan, and machine translations are labelled.

With a 90-day paid pilot on one live decision, priced below typical low-value purchase limits. We set up your city from your public documents, your staff review and publish, and you get a short report you can take to council.
